children: fell 14.25% premarket after second quarter results that beat on both lines. Revenue rose 30% to $771.8 million against the $735.01
million consensus, and non-GAAP earnings came in at $1.90 a share versus $1.62 expected. Non-GAAP operating margin widened to 24% from 15% a year earlier.

Atlas, the cloud database business, grew about 29% for a fifth consecutive quarter and added a record $127 million in year-over-year revenue. Enterprise Advanced and other revenue rose 36%. Remaining performance obligations climbed 91% to $1.52 billion, net ARR expansion reached 122%, and free cash flow nearly doubled to $137.6 million. The company added 2,900 net new customers. Stock-based compensation ran $148.9 million in the quarter.

MongoDB raised full-year revenue guidance to $2.99 billion to $3.03 billion and lifted its non-GAAP operating income outlook to $616.3 million to $636.3 million. The third quarter guide is where the tone changes. Atlas growth is expected at roughly 26%, and on a GAAP basis the company guided to an operating loss of $10.5 million to $14.5 million for the quarter and up to $28 million for the year.

title: MongoDB Beat, Raised, and Fell 14%
